instructions:
You were seen today for a small lesion on your lower lip and for comprehensive screening for sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

The lip lesion was evaluated today. Because the exact cause of the lesion has not been confirmed, it is currently being documented as a lip lesion (K13.0) rather than a confirmed herpes infection.

Testing

STI testing was collected/ordered today as discussed. We will contact you when your laboratory results are available and provide additional recommendations or treatment if indicated based on the results.

Please understand that some infections may not become detectable immediately after a recent exposure. Depending on the timing of your most recent sexual exposure and today's results, repeat testing may occasionally be recommended.

Lip Care
Keep the affected area clean and avoid picking, squeezing, or repeatedly touching the lesion.
Avoid licking or otherwise irritating the area while it heals.
Wash your hands after touching the lesion.
Until the cause is known and the lesion has completely healed, avoid kissing and oral sexual contact to reduce the possibility of transmitting an infection if the lesion is infectious.
Do not share lip products, drinks, eating utensils, razors, or other personal items that contact the mouth.
While Awaiting STI Results

Use condoms or other appropriate barrier protection during sexual activity while awaiting your results. If any testing returns positive, we will discuss treatment, partner notification/testing when appropriate, and any recommended follow-up testing.

Follow-Up

<clinic> will contact you once your laboratory results are received.

Return for reevaluation if the lip lesion becomes larger, increasingly painful, develops additional blisters or ulcers, repeatedly returns, or fails to heal.

Seek prompt medical attention if you develop significant facial or lip swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, high fever, severe pain, eye involvement, a widespread rash, genital sores, abnormal vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, or other concerning new symptoms.
